Technicians are trained on specific injector lines and turbos, and most remanufactured injectors receive new trim code programming. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

While the company does not list specific industry verticals, its product range serves the diesel repair and maintenance market, including heavy-duty trucking, construction equipment, agricultural machinery, and fleet maintenance operations.

DTIS Techs emphasizes quality through specialized technician training and trim code programming on injectors. It backs products with a standard 12-month, unlimited-mileage warranty, an optional 18-month extended warranty, free ground shipping, and a 45-day core return policy for core charge refunds.

about:
DZEE Textiles LLC operates from Orlando, Florida, where it was established more than 25 years ago as a wholesale distributor of hotel supplies. The company began with a vision to provide high-quality, affordable hospitality products directly to the industry, bypassing intermediaries.

The company distributes a broad range of hospitality goods — bath linens, pool and gym towels, bed sheets, pillow cases, duvets, blankets, decorative bedding, bath amenities, guest-room appliances, and janitorial supplies. It sources products using what it describes as state-of-the-art technology and applies rigorous quality-control measures. DZEE Textiles reports serving more than 10,000 customers, including hotels, motels, resorts, vacation rentals, salons, and casinos, and emphasizes direct factory pricing with free delivery on orders over $999 in most areas.

Its customer base spans the hospitality sector, specifically hotels, motels, resorts, vacation rentals, salons, and casinos. The company highlights long-standing relationships with hospitality buyers and hotel managers built on trust and mutual respect.

DZEE Textiles says it differentiates itself through unbeatable prices, high durability, and fast, free delivery. It also points to eco-friendly manufacturing processes and sustainable material sourcing as part of its commitment to responsible business practices.

about:
Daedalus Industrial is based in Easley, South Carolina. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders.

The company manufactures custom control panels through build-to-print and custom design services, with in-house fabrication optimized for rapid deployment. It delivers automation solutions including SCADA and IoT system development, robotic integration with collaborative robotics and vision systems, modular motion and process control, and advanced analytics with AI-driven predictive maintenance and adaptive machine vision. Daedalus also operates as a licensed electrical contractor specializing in low- and ultra-low-voltage systems, building management systems, power management, structured cabling, and industrial networking. Additional capabilities encompass OT cybersecurity risk assessments, secure architecture design, network segmentation, compliance audits aligned with NIST and IEC 62443, and controls-centric installation services for third-party OEM equipment.

Daedalus serves data centers, utilities, industrial infrastructure, and manufacturing sectors, providing mission-critical solutions for high-availability environments. Its customer base includes original equipment manufacturers and capital project teams seeking turnkey automation, from prototype through production.

The company emphasizes right-sized, future-proof engineering that balances efficiency with efficacy, avoiding unnecessary complexity. Its differentiators include modular, scalable designs, in-house data science expertise for lean AI integration, and a responsive, agile approach to custom fabrication and controls engineering.

name: Dakota Carding
old_description: offers you custom fiber processing of your wool, animal fibers, exotics and misc. fibers. This is a cottage industry carding mill providing you with affordable custom washing and carding of your animal/plant/pet fibers.
about:
Dakota Carding operates as a cottage industry carding mill in Groton, South Dakota, specializing in custom fiber processing for individual producers and fiber artists. The company, also known as Dakota Carding & Wool Co., processes wool, animal fibers, exotic fibers, and plant-based materials through washing and carding services.

Its core operations center on a Dyna Card Mill that provides custom washing and carding of customer-supplied fibers. In addition to contract processing, the mill produces its own carded wool blends, handspun and millspun yarns, and sheepskins. The facility also retails spinning wheels, looms, knitting needles, and finished wearable art under the Biotayarns label. All fibers are sourced domestically, with an emphasis on local prairie-inspired color blends.

The customer base includes hand spinners, felters, and small-scale fiber producers seeking affordable custom carding for their own clips, as well as hobbyists purchasing ready-to-spin blends and equipment. The mill serves both individual fiber growers who send in raw fleece and retail customers looking for unique yarns and spinning supplies.

The business highlights its affordable, small-batch processing and domestic sourcing as key differentiators. The current owners have listed the carding mill for sale, indicating a transition opportunity for the operation.

name: Dakota Timber Company - Sustainable Wood Products & Home Goods - Made In the USA
old_description: Our lumber materials are sourced primarily from agricultural buildings in the upper Midwest or from urban tree removals.
about:
Dakota Timber Company operates from Horace, North Dakota, where it produces a line of reclaimed wood products for residential and commercial projects. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but its roots are tied to the upper Midwest's agricultural heritage.

The shop manufactures fireplace mantels, floating shelf kits, structural beams, shiplap paneling, stair treads, brackets, and custom tops. Lumber is sourced primarily from decommissioned agricultural buildings across the upper Midwest and from urban tree removals, then milled and finished in-house. Production is made-to-order with a typical lead time of four to six weeks, and finished goods ship via LTL freight.

Customers include homeowners, builders, and interior designers across the region. Recent project work includes floating shelf installations for Rachel Platt of RP at Home, a fireplace mantel for D Gilpin Properties, white oak shiplap for Klein Custom Homes, and a whole-home package for Studio West's Rose Creek residence in Fargo, North Dakota.

The company positions its output as 100 percent American-made, emphasizing low-impact production and the reuse of materials that would otherwise enter the waste stream. Its floating shelf kits feature a proprietary mounting bracket designed for straightforward installation.

name: Danfoss Power Solutions
old_description: We engineer solutions that increase machine productivity, reduce emissions, lower energy consumption, and enable electrification.
about:
Danfoss Power Solutions operates from Searcy, Arkansas, as part of a global enterprise founded in 1933 by Mads Clausen in Denmark. The company remains family-owned, a structure it says underpins long-term value creation for stakeholders.

The business runs three core segments. Danfoss Power Solutions delivers mobile and industrial hydraulics, fluid conveyance, data-center thermal management, electrification systems, and software. Danfoss Climate Solutions provides energy-efficient heating and cooling for industrial plants, buildings, infrastructure, data centers, and the cold chain. Danfoss Power Electronics and Drives produces power semiconductor modules, variable-speed drives, and power-conversion equipment. Innovation is vetted through 13 Application Development Centers worldwide where customers test solutions in live environments.

Customers span mobile machinery, industrial automation, data-center operators, construction, commercial refrigeration, and general industrial markets. Publicly cited collaborations include an energy-efficient AI supercomputer with HPE and a 30 percent energy-saving project with Smardt for chiller systems.

Danfoss states its engineering focus is on increasing machine productivity, cutting emissions, lowering energy consumption, and enabling electrification. The family ownership model, it says, allows massive reinvestment in innovation and digitalization while maintaining a philanthropic commitment through its foundations.

name: Dangar Engineering & Mfg.
old_description: Dangar Engineering specializes in large precision CNC machining, including 5-axis milling of complex parts and tooling. Products serve aerospace, automotive, medical and commercial industries.
about:
Dangar Engineering & Mfg. has operated from Ventura, California since its founding in 1954. The company was established with a focus on mastering the edge of machining technology, choosing to specialize in the difficult and unusual parts that other shops could not produce.

The shop provides large precision CNC machining, including 5-axis milling of complex parts, tooling, prototypes, and production runs. Its equipment includes 5-axis machines with a 242-inch by 115-inch by 25-inch machining envelope (part envelope up to 242 by 115 by 72 inches) and a coordinate measuring machine with a 161.75 by 54 by 53.375-inch inspection envelope, all housed in a 24-hour temperature-controlled facility. Design and NC programming are performed using CATIA CAD/CAM. The company employs 50 to 99 people and also offers inspection, reverse engineering, complex assemblies, welding, and fabrication.

Dangar serves aerospace, architectural, automotive, commercial, medical, and marine industries. Its customer approvals include Northrop Grumman, Lockheed Martin, Litton, Volvo, BMW, Volkswagen, and Pilkington Aerospace. Machined parts are used in commercial and military aerospace applications as well as titanium components implanted in the human body.

The company's stated philosophy is to be a reliable source of high-precision, close-tolerance products with exceptional quality, positioning itself as a one-stop shop for any-angle 5-axis holes and very complex geometry.

about:
Dar Collision Parts is a family-owned-and-operated distributor of automotive collision parts based in St. Albans, West Virginia. Founded in 1991, the company has over three decades of experience in the auto body parts service industry.

The company operates as a distributor of replacement collision parts, including rust repair panels, grilles, bumpers, fenders, header panels, bedsides, doors, and headlight bezels. It also supplies a comprehensive line of automotive exterior lighting as a distributor of TYC and Globe Lighting products, stocking headlights, sidemarkers, park lamps, and taillights for many cars and trucks. In addition, Dar Collision Parts carries a range of truck and SUV accessories such as nerf bars, bedliners, tonneau covers, custom cowl hoods, bug shields, headlight and taillight covers, stepmates, aluminum bed protection, and tool boxes. The firm purchases directly from numerous manufacturers and maintains a large in-stock inventory.

Dar Collision Parts serves the automotive aftermarket, primarily collision repair shops, auto body shops, and truck and SUV owners seeking replacement parts and accessories. Its product range addresses needs from accident-related body panel replacement to lighting upgrades and accessory installation.

The company emphasizes providing superior quality at a lower cost to the automotive aftermarket, leveraging direct manufacturer relationships and a large in-stock inventory to meet customer needs promptly.

name: Darn It Inc
old_description: offered by Darn It! From Storage to Inventory Management and Logistics, We do it all!
about:
Darn It! Inc. operates from New Bedford, Massachusetts, where it was established in 1996 by Jeff Glassman. Glassman launched the business after his family’s apparel factory lost the majority of its workforce to lower-cost competitors in Mexico; a former customer asked him to repair 30,000 damaged trousers, prompting the creation of a company focused on refurbishing clothing. The firm remains family-run.

The company provides warehousing, distribution, and refurbishment services. Its quality-control offerings include 100% inspection of soft lines and hard goods, labeling, sewing repairs, button and snap replacement, cleaning (with an ozone room for odor removal), laundering, mold remediation, pressing, packaging, kitting, and reverse logistics such as returns processing and restocking. The warehouse and distribution arm accounts for roughly 40 percent of revenue and serves more than 20 clients, handling merchandise that ranges from apparel to books and watches.

Customers include retailers, manufacturers, wholesalers, and web-based businesses worldwide. In one case, Darn It! corrected 1,200 mislabeled shirts for a retailer; in another, it inspected 8,000 sets of blackout curtains, recovering 91 percent as sellable inventory through inspection, sewing repairs, and spot cleaning.

Glassman started the business to fill a gap in repairing damaged goods from overseas production, and the company emphasizes quick turnaround to support lean inventory programs for its clients.

about:
Days Custom Design is a family-owned custom printing and personalization company based in Casper, Wyoming. Founded in 2020 by Robert, Kathy, and Nevaeh Day, the business was started to help customers turn ideas into high-quality products with personal, dependable service.

The shop provides a range of decoration services including screen printing and direct-to-film transfers for apparel, embroidery for hats and garments, laser engraving on drinkware and wood items, and large-format output such as banners, decals, and storefront window graphics. They also supply promotional products, uniforms, and personalized gifts, serving both local clients in Natrona County and customers nationwide through shipping.

Their customer base spans businesses, schools, sports teams, community organizations, events, and individuals. Past projects include rush shirts for a world-record camp, engraved water bottles for a real estate team, branded drinkware for a medical practice, and custom apparel for a barbecue restaurant. The company works with orders ranging from single personalized gifts to coordinated programs for entire organizations.

Days Custom Design emphasizes a collaborative, honest, and straightforward approach, guiding clients through design and production. The business has been recognized locally, winning Oil City's Best Locally Owned Business in 2025 and Best Customer Service in 2026, reflecting its focus on responsive communication and reliable turnaround.

about:
Dayton Plastics, located in Dayton, Tennessee, was founded in 1988 with a vision of providing quality molded products in the USA at an affordable price. The company has grown to become one of the largest custom injection molders in the Southeast.

The company operates a 25,000-square-foot manufacturing and warehousing facility housing 15 injection molding machines with clamping forces from 85 to 1,000 tons. It produces parts ranging from less than one gram to 10 pounds, and offers product development, assembly, packaging, and shipping services. The team also assists customers with mold design and runs existing customer-owned molds.

Dayton Plastics serves the HVAC and hot water heater sectors for residential and recreational vehicle markets, and also molds components for pool products, gardening products, and carpet manufacturing equipment. Its customer base includes both large-volume OEMs and individuals needing smaller runs.

The business was started to deliver American-made molded parts at competitive prices, and it emphasizes guiding projects from concept through production with quick quoting on both new and existing molds.

about:
DeVo's WoodCraft operates from Eagle River, Alaska, where founder Kris DeVo produces custom furniture and finished wood goods. DeVo's woodworking roots trace to junior high, when a shop teacher inspired him to win first place at the California State Fair and launch his own woodshop at age 13. After moving to Alaska in 2009 and marrying in 2011, he continued the craft in his current location.

The shop offers custom furniture fabrication, countertops, kitchen islands, and tables, along with a line of finished products that includes cutting boards, butcher blocks, bowls, kitchen and hunting knives, coasters, knife blocks, pen blanks, and stabilized wood blanks. In-house capabilities cover milling and lamination services by appointment, as well as delivery and installation for larger pieces.

The business serves individual customers, woodworkers, and knife makers seeking custom wood components and finished goods. Concrete examples from the product list show a focus on kitchen and outdoor cutlery accessories, as well as maker supplies such as pen blanks and burl.

DeVo cites his early passion for woodworking and the influence of his junior-high teacher as the reason he started the shop, describing the venture as a place where his passions for woodcraft, photography, and videography come together.

old_description: Authentic recipes made with real ingredients, slow-cooked with tradition and ready when you are.
about:
Del Real Foods operates from Moore, Oklahoma, where it was founded on a dream of sharing authentic Hispanic flavors made with love. The company traces its roots to humble beginnings, aiming to bring traditional recipes like tamales, carnitas, and pupusas to family tables across America.

The manufacturer produces a wide range of Mexican and Central American foods, including carnitas, barbacoa, shredded and pulled chicken, birria, chile verde, pork al pastor, and various tamale and pupusa varieties, along with fire-roasted salsas, Mexican rice, and refried beans. All items are slow-cooked using traditional methods with fresh ingredients and no preservatives, designed to deliver homemade taste ready in minutes.

Del Real Foods sells its products through grocery retail channels, making them available at local grocery stores nationwide. The company focuses on the consumer packaged goods sector, supplying retailers who cater to shoppers seeking authentic Hispanic cuisine.

The business was built to share authentic Hispanic flavors inspired by generations of homemade cooking, emphasizing traditional preparation, fresh ingredients, and the absence of preservatives as its defining difference.

Delicious New Mexico operates from Albuquerque in Bernalillo County, New Mexico. The initiative was developed through the Hispanic-American Institute under a USDA/AMS grant and is a program of the Rio Grande Community Development Corporation, a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization. While a precise founding year is not published, the team notes nearly 20 years of experience working with food businesses across the state.

The organization runs a fleet of refrigerated vehicles on weekly statewide routes, picking up from multiple farms on a single trip to consolidate loads and reduce costs. Services include scheduled pick-up and delivery for a flat fee, assistance with wholesale packaging and pricing, and retail placement coordination. Three staff members are listed as contacts: a director of finance and programs, a facilities manager, and a project coordinator.

Delicious New Mexico serves small and mid-sized farms, food producers, and retail outlets throughout New Mexico. Customers include Legacy Acres Farm in Tucumcari, which moved 100 pounds of cabbage to Meals on Wheels; Dulce Tradición, which placed biscuits in retail stores; and the Agri-cultura Network, a collective of farms that pools products for processing and distribution in Bernalillo County.

The initiative was created because transporting produce during planting and harvest seasons pulls farmers away from core work, incurs fuel and vehicle expenses, and often requires multiple trips or half-full trucks. By consolidating shipments and providing daily refrigerated transport, Delicious New Mexico aims to save producers time and money while strengthening local food distribution.

old_description: Our updated platform offers streamlined access to RF designs across nearly 100 interfaces. We will consistently add new products, so check back often for the latest design resources.
about:
Delta Electronics Manufacturing Corporation operates from Beverly, Massachusetts. The company traces its roots back over 65 years, having evolved from a small manufacturing business into a global provider of RF, microwave, and millimeter-wave solutions. No founding year or founder names are disclosed, and ownership structure is not specified.

Delta designs and manufactures RF connectors, adapters, and cable assemblies across nearly 100 interface types, covering frequencies from DC to 67.5 GHz for connectors and 13.56 MHz to 65 GHz for cables. Its Advanced Vertically Integrated (AVI) facilities handle the full production chain in-house: design and simulation, precision machining, soldering, plating, assembly, and testing — including insertion loss, return loss, phase, and delay verification. The company also produces semi-rigid and flexible cable equivalents, high-power cables, high-frequency test cables, and accessories such as keying baskets, dust caps, and custom hardware.

Delta serves military, aerospace, communications, broadcast and audio, test and measurement, and semiconductor industries. As a longtime QPL supplier qualified to MIL-PRF-55339, it provides interconnects for military aircraft, satellite launch vehicles, and missiles. Aerospace programs use its components in commercial aircraft, drones, and satellites. Communications customers include two-way radio, base station, and antenna system manufacturers. Broadcast and audio applications span in-ear monitors, broadcast infrastructure, and alert systems. Test and measurement clients range from semiconductor chip makers to RF calibration labs. In the semiconductor sector, Delta's interconnects appear in etch equipment, deposition tools, and chip testers.

The company emphasizes its "Delta Difference" — vertically integrated facilities that control the entire manufacturing process from raw stock to finished product, enabling quick, cost-effective delivery of high-performance customized solutions. Reliability, durability, and performance are cited as the drivers behind this integration.

name: Department of Food Science and Technology
old_description: The Forefront of Safe and Sustainable Food for a Healthier World
about:
The Department of Food Science and Technology operates from Corvallis, Oregon, as part of Oregon State University’s College of Agricultural Sciences. A public institution, the department has no single founder but traces its roots to the university’s land-grant mission in agricultural research and education.

The department provides a suite of technical services for the food and beverage sector, including flavor analysis, food microbiology and safety testing, pilot-scale manufacturing, product and process development, quality and shelf-life evaluation, and sensory and consumer testing. Its pilot manufacturing facility supports small-batch production for product validation, while specialized service lines address beer, wine, dairy, seafood, and general food and beverage categories.

Clients range from startups to established processors in the Pacific Northwest and beyond. The department collaborates with industry partners such as Scott Labs on beer spoilage prevention and conducts research on smoke impact for Oregon wine grape growers. It also serves as the Western Regional Center to Enhance Food Safety (WRCEFS), delivering FSMA training to small and mid-sized farms, processors, and wholesalers across 13 western states and two territories.

What distinguishes the department is its integration of academic research, extension outreach, and fee-for-service testing under one roof. The WRCEFS designation, backed by a USDA-NIFA grant, positions it as a hub for food safety training, while its pilot plant and sensory labs allow companies to de-risk new products before full-scale commercialization.

about:
Dielectric Manufacturing operates from a 100,000-square-foot headquarters in Richfield, Wisconsin, just northwest of Milwaukee, with additional production plants in Waupaca, Wisconsin; Lake Mills, Iowa; and Richmond, Illinois. The company traces its roots to 1966 when Ray Esser founded Dielectric Corporation in central Wisconsin. The Esser family retains private ownership, and the name was updated to Dielectric Manufacturing in 2019 to reflect expanded capabilities beyond plastics into metal machining and carbon fiber composites.

The firm functions as a single-source contract manufacturer, handling design collaboration, prototyping, machining, fabrication, welding, finishing, assembly, kitting, packaging, and inventory management. Its equipment roster includes vertical and horizontal machining centers, 5-axis milling, 6-axis laser cutting, routing, stamping, turning, bending, cold forming, and plastic and metal welding. The Richfield facility opened in 2020; the Waupaca site specializes in ferrous metals, while the Richmond location, acquired in October 2025 as EMS Industrial & Service Co., produces busbars. All three Wisconsin and Iowa plants hold ISO 9001:2015 certification, and the Waupaca operation maintains ITAR registration through the DDTC.

Customers span aerospace, agriculture, defense, electrical, food processing, gas and oil, health care and medical equipment, power generation and distribution (including wind), power sports, marine, and data centers. The client base ranges from small businesses to Fortune 500 companies such as Eaton Corporation's Power Systems Division. Dielectric also distributes unfinished thermoplastics, thermosets, ferrous and non-ferrous metals, and carbon fiber composites in sheet, rod, tube, and block forms.

The company emphasizes a partner-oriented approach, offering material selection guidance and design-for-manufacturability input to reduce cost and lead time. Standard lead times are quoted at two weeks, with expedited turnaround demonstrated on urgent orders. ITAR compliance and ongoing CMMC 2.0 implementation support defense-sector work.

Domico Med-Device is based in Fenton, Michigan. The company became an independent business after spinning out of a larger organization, driven by a vision to serve as a supplier of high-quality medical products worldwide.

Its vertically integrated capabilities include compression molding, foam fabrication, machining, tool design and build, sewing, sealing, coating, vacuum forming, and final product assembly. Domico serves healthcare professionals, distributors, OEMs, and product inventors in the medical device industry. Its product portfolio includes MRI positioning aids, operating room cord management and arm positioning devices, and a range of table pads designed for secure support and pressure relief. The company also provides contract manufacturing of components and assemblies for medical device OEMs.

Domico emphasizes its vertically integrated model—taking products from concept to market under one roof—to streamline timelines, reduce risk, and ensure consistency. The company states its mission is to empower healthcare innovation by delivering reliable, compliant manufacturing solutions that improve patient outcomes and enhance operational efficiency.

about:
Dutchland Plastics has operated from Oostburg, Wisconsin since 1967, building a rotational molding business that now spans a nearly 200,000-square-foot facility there and a second plant in Canastota, New York.

The firm specializes in high-volume rotational molding of large plastic parts, producing pieces up to 500 pounds and 17 feet long. Its capabilities cover the full product lifecycle: design and engineering, foam filling, mold-in graphics, robotic and CNC trimming, assembly, and warehousing and distribution. Materials processed include polyethylene, flexible PVC, nylon, and EVA.

Dutchland serves recreational, commercial, outdoor, food and beverage, furniture, marine, and industrial markets. Typical products include kayaks, coolers, jungle gyms, and rotomolded furniture for marine and watercraft applications.

The company positions itself as a turnkey partner for oversized custom projects, emphasizing a "QuickConnect" onboarding program designed to transition production without interruption. Its stated focus is on clients who need to make something really big, offering engineering through to finished-goods shipping under one roof.

about:
Based in Yankton, South Dakota, Dynamic Cable & Security LLC draws on more than two decades of field experience in low-voltage systems. The company was founded by a technician who spent 20 years working on fiber optic construction, CCTV, security cameras, audio and video systems, and low-voltage wiring across the Kansas City metro area before returning to Yankton to serve the region.

The firm provides full-service low-voltage solutions, including security camera system design, installation, and maintenance for analog and IP networks; fiber optic splicing, testing, termination, and emergency repair for both aerial and underground plant; whole-home and commercial audio/video design and installation, from home theaters to multi-zone distributed systems and custom display walls; and mobile solar-powered CCTV trailers equipped with 8MP PTZ cameras and license-plate recognition, available for sale or rent. The team reports more than 500 completed jobs and offers 24/7 on-call support across a 250-mile radius covering South Dakota, Nebraska, and Iowa.

Customers range from single-family homes and apartment complexes to farms, commercial businesses, colleges, public schools, and government facilities. The company’s fiber optic services also support telecommunications carriers needing outage response and routine terminations.

Dynamic Cable & Security emphasizes a "big city solutions with a small town feel" approach, backing its security camera installations with a minimum five-year warranty and highlighting its ability to handle everything from routine terminations to complex fiber restoration using specialized tools and hands-on expertise.

about:
E-Tronix operates from St. Louis Park, Minnesota, as a manufacturers' representative firm covering the Upper Midwest. The company was founded by Erik Stromberg, who had worked for several representative firms in the region since 1998 before launching E-Tronix under the Stromberg Company banner. Stromberg, a University of North Dakota graduate, built the business around a client-first approach and deep industry relationships.

Rather than manufacturing products, E-Tronix represents equipment and materials suppliers for electronics assembly, wire and cable processing, and medical device manufacturing. Its line card includes the LPMS Kappa 1100H low-pressure molding system, Elmotec SolderSmart TOP robotic soldering cells, Hakko FX-971 precision hand-soldering stations, KIC thermal profiling tools, and Nathan Trotter solder alloys. A seven-person team — including a solutions engineer with Daktronics experience and a former Navy electrician's mate who specialized in selective soldering at Pillarhouse — provides technical support, equipment evaluation, and process consulting across Minnesota, the Dakotas, Wisconsin, Iowa, Illinois, Kansas, Missouri, Indiana, and Kentucky.

The firm serves electronic assembly houses, wire-harness shops, and medical-device OEMs. Named references include Daktronics, where Dave Philips credited E-Tronix with guiding equipment selection and implementation, and ProActive PCB, where Paul Schwanbeck highlighted the team's ability to escalate issues through its manufacturer network. E-Tronix also hosts technical webinars on topics such as automatic thermal profiling and next-generation PCB complexity, and exhibits at events like the SMTA Wisconsin Expo and the Electrical Wire Processing Technology Expo.

The company states its differentiation lies in "Partnership," "Solutions Expertise," and "Customer Focus" — summarized as listening and responding in a timely fashion.

EBRO serves the retail grocery trade, supplying Hispanic food products to supermarkets and specialty stores throughout the Midwest. The company describes itself as one of the largest minority-owned food manufacturers in the region.

The Abreu family emphasizes its generational expertise and pioneering role in setting benchmarks for original Hispanic food products.

name: ECM USA
old_description: Lab, university, and research & development heat treat solutions for semiconductor wafer processing
about:
ECM USA operates from Pleasant Prairie, Wisconsin, positioned between Milwaukee and Chicago. The company serves as the American subsidiary of the France-based ECM Group, which consolidates thermal, gas, and atmosphere management expertise across multiple brands headquartered near Grenoble and Montpellier. ECM USA established its Synergy Center in Pleasant Prairie in 2018, housing a NANO vacuum furnace for on-site process development and metallurgical testing.

The company designs and manufactures vacuum furnace systems using cold-wall, electric heating technology that eliminates open flames and enables higher temperature treatments with easy integration into machining lines. Its furnace portfolio includes the ECO double-chamber, JUMBO high-volume, FLEX modular, NANO small-batch, VESUVE nitriding/FNC, FULGURA multi-flow, TURQUOISE horizontal, LILLIPUT hearth-lift, CRISTAL bell, and PFTH vertical oil-quench models, with maximum work zones up to 1,500 mm and load capacities to 2,000 kg. Core processes cover low-pressure vacuum carburizing (LPC), carbonitriding, brazing, sintering, vacuum induction melting, vacuum arc remelting, tempering, vacuum purged gas nitriding, ferritic nitrocarburizing, and vapor-phase aluminizing. Through the ECM Greentech division, it supplies semiconductor wafer-processing furnaces for diffusion, oxidation, doping, and rapid thermal processing up to 300 mm wafers, plus silicon ingot casting and crystal growth equipment. ECM Robotics provides automation integration ranging from cleanroom wafer handling to heavy automotive loads exceeding 1,000 kg.

ECM USA serves the automotive, aerospace, marine, agricultural, semiconductor, solar/photovoltaic, and general industrial heat-treat sectors, as well as university and R&D laboratories. Customers in the United States, Canada, and Mexico include EV transmission manufacturers using LPC, semiconductor fabs requiring wafer processing and SiC crystal growth, and solar producers casting PV silicon ingots. The Synergy Center allows prospective buyers to run low-pressure carburizing and high-pressure gas quenching trials with on-site CMM dimensional measurement, 3D microscopy, and hardness testing before committing to a system purchase.

The company emphasizes that its cold-wall vacuum technology prevents inter-granular oxidation during carburizing, minimizes energy consumption and CO2 emissions, and improves metallurgical properties and process repeatability. Field service, installation, training, and aftermarket parts availability are positioned as integral to the offering, supported by the ECM Group's 50-plus years of engineering and design experience.

old_description: Do to national material shortages, some parts may take longer to ship.
about:
EDCOR Electronics Corporation operates from Carlsbad, New Mexico, where it has been based since January 1991. The company traces its roots to the early 1960s in Utah, where it began as Electronic Development Corporation, a public firm that pioneered wireless microphones and held the first U.S. patent in that field. After several ownership changes and relocations — through Costa Mesa, Irvine, and Santa Ana, California — the management team bought out all shareholders in late 1990, financed the move to New Mexico, and reincorporated the business there.

The company designs and manufactures a broad line of transformers and related components. Its catalog includes audio matching transformers (microphone, line level, combiners, splitters), audio distribution transformers, stereo-to-mono couplers, classic tube audio transformers (single-ended, push-pull, interstage), power transformers for tube and solid-state equipment, chokes and inductors (DC power chokes, high-voltage plate/filament), and a range of parts such as coil bobbins (nylon 6/6 glass-filled), steel laminations, end bells, brackets, and mounting hardware. EDCOR also offers custom transformer design and sells amplifier replacement transformers and kit transformers for brands such as Fender, Dynaco, and Decware.

EDCOR serves professional audio installers, musicians, amplifier builders, and hobbyists. Its distribution transformers were used in the refit of the Rose Bowl in the mid-to-late 1980s. Current customers include tube amplifier designers like Pete Millett and Bruce Heran (OddWatt), kit builders (Decware ZEN kits), and repair shops needing replacements for vintage Fender, Dynaco, and other amplifiers. The company also supports the DIY community with technical blogs and design resources.

EDCOR emphasizes domestic manufacturing: "Proudly designed and built in 'MERICA," with a stated effort to source materials and parts from U.S. suppliers. The transformer production process has evolved over four decades, originally driven by the company's own difficulty in obtaining quality audio and power transformers in the early 1980s, which led to the acquisition of Delta Magnetics and its manufacturing facilities.

EIC Semiconductor Inc is headquartered in Irwindale, California. The company operates as a manufacturer of discrete semiconductor devices.

EIC provides end-to-end manufacturing with a dedicated wafer fabrication facility and assembly plant, allowing control over quality and supply. The company produces a broad portfolio of discrete semiconductors, including Zener diodes, switching diodes, rectifier diodes, transient voltage suppressors (TVS), thyristors, and small-signal transistors. Its catalog encompasses over 15,000 part numbers across more than 50 package types. TVS devices range from 150 W to 50,000 W, while silicon rectifier diodes offer avalanche voltages up to 2,500 V and reverse voltages up to 3,000 V, with AEC-Q101 qualification. High-voltage ultra-fast recovery rectifiers are available with reverse voltages from 7,500 V to 12,000 V.

The company serves automotive electronics, automotive rectifier diodes, aviation, medical, power supply, industrial electronics, and consumer electronics markets.

EIC emphasizes its integrated wafer fab and assembly operations as a means to ensure quality control and supply continuity, supported by what it describes as powerful research capabilities.

ELIS Manufacturing & Packaging Solutions operates from a single facility in Kaufman, Texas. The company began at a family kitchen table in Kaufman and has spent the last decade growing into a contract manufacturer whose clients’ products appear on shelves across the United States and internationally. It remains family-owned and founder-led, with Keith Vinson serving as owner and CEO; the name honors his grandfather, Ellis, whose work ethic the company says guides its operations.

ELIS provides turnkey contract manufacturing and packaging for nutraceuticals and consumables. Its services span product development, ingredient sourcing, blending, encapsulation, flavoring and formulating, filling (bottles, pouches, sachets, stick packs), printing (roll stock, pouch, screen printing on bottles), kitting, fulfillment, warehousing and shipping. The facility handles powders, liquids, creams, gels, tablets and capsules, and the company notes it applies the same quality standards to runs as small as 2,000 units and as large as 200,000 units.

The company serves brands in the nutraceutical, beauty and cosmetics, food and beverage, pet food and sports nutrition categories. Its customers include brands such as TryCinny.com, STROKESGAINED, Freedom Tea Co, Glucose SOS and Nutra Coast, whose products are stocked by major retailers nationwide.

ELIS was created after its founders experienced unreliable co-packers while launching their own product line. They built the company to offer a design-to-delivery partner under one roof, with a dedicated project manager who knows each product’s timeline and launch window, and a team that treats every client’s product as its own.

ETEMCO was established in 1952 in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, by four entrepreneurs who set out to design and manufacture test equipment for the RCA picture tube factory. The business expanded from that initial contract into a full-service electronic and electromechanical manufacturing company, and it has remained in Lancaster for over seven decades.

The company provides printed circuit board assembly services from prototype through production, specializing in high-mix, low-to-medium volume runs typically ranging from fewer than 100 units to 25,000 units depending on complexity. Its capabilities include surface-mount technology (SMT) with high-speed pick-and-place equipment, through-hole assembly, selective soldering, automated optical inspection (2D and 3D AOI), conformal coating and RTV dispensing via a PVA Delta 8 four-axis system, and PDR infrared rework for non-contact component repair. The firm emphasizes a seamless prototype-to-production transition and invests heavily in advanced equipment to maintain quality.

ETEMCO serves customers in medical and healthcare (diagnostic imaging, implantable devices), telecommunications and networking (network infrastructure, wireless communication), industrial automation and controls, military and law enforcement, transportation and mobility (automotive, aerospace, maritime), and security and access control (motion sensors, security sensors, linear drives). The company also supports broadcast equipment and asset tracking applications.

Founded on a mission of innovation and precision, ETEMCO differentiates itself through a quality-driven culture, on-time delivery focus, and responsive communication. The company states that quality drives its entire operation, from skilled production teams and precise component placement to stringent quality control, and it prioritizes efficiency without sacrificing quality to meet tight deadlines.

East Penn Manufacturing, a private, family-owned company, was founded in 1946 by Air Force veteran DeLight Breidegam Jr. and his father, DeLight Sr., in a one-room creamery in Bowers, Pennsylvania. The business began by rebuilding used batteries to meet post-war demand from returning GIs. In 1947, Karl Gasche joined as a partner, and the Deka brand—derived from "DeLight" and "Karl"—was born. Today the company operates a major battery finishing and distribution plant in Temple, Texas, alongside what it describes as the world's largest single-site lead battery manufacturing facility.

East Penn produces lead-acid batteries for automotive, industrial, motive power, transportation, and reserve power (UPS, telecommunications, renewable energy) applications. Its product portfolio spans 515 designs, supported by vertically integrated operations that include wire and cable manufacturing, battery accessories, and custom solutions. The company reports over 10,500 full-time employees worldwide and operates through divisions such as Motive Power, Transportation, Reserve Power, and Wire & Cable, as well as subsidiaries including Navitas Systems (lithium technology), MK Battery, East Penn Canada, and East Penn International.

Customers span automotive OEMs, material-handling equipment makers, commercial truck fleets, telecommunications providers, and renewable-energy integrators. The company has been recognized by Honda and John Deere for supplier sustainability, and its batteries serve applications ranging from lift trucks and commercial vehicles to critical backup power for data centers and outside plant.

The founding principle of putting customers and employees first remains central, reinforced by an integrated quality and environmental management system. East Penn emphasizes pollution prevention, waste reduction, and compliance with global standards, holding multiple internationally recognized certifications. A $110 million expansion announced for the Texas facility in 2026 underscores continued investment in domestic capacity.

name: Eatem Foods Co
old_description: ADM connects harvest to home, utilizing our farmer partnerships, global transportation capabilities, market insights, and innovation to deliver solutions today and tomorrow.
about:
Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, ADM operates as a global agricultural supply chain manager and processor. The company purchases crops from tens of thousands of farmers worldwide, moves them through an integrated network of elevators, trucks, railcars, barges, and ships, and transforms them at 325 production sites into ingredients for food, feed, fuel, and industrial uses. A founding year and original founders are not disclosed in its public materials; the business is a publicly traded corporation.

ADM’s core activities span crop origination, transportation logistics, and large-scale ingredient manufacturing. Its human nutrition portfolio includes colors, flavors, proteins, and texturants for beverages, baked goods, and supplements. Animal nutrition covers complete feeds, premixes, and additives for livestock, aquaculture, and pets. The industrial biosolutions segment produces biofuels, bioplastics, and bio-based chemicals. In 2024 the company moved 140 million metric tons of agricultural products — roughly 5% of global trade — and generated $85 billion in revenue with 44,000 employees across six continents.

Customers range from multinational food and beverage brands to feed mills, pet food manufacturers, and industrial companies seeking renewable alternatives. ADM serves the human nutrition, animal nutrition, pet nutrition, and industrial biosolutions markets, with specific applications in beverages, bakery, dietary supplements, aquaculture feed, biodiesel, personal care, and home care products.

The company emphasizes its farmer partnerships, regenerative agriculture programs, and precision fermentation capabilities as differentiators. It positions itself as a leader in business-driven sustainability, leveraging its unmatched transportation network and manufacturing footprint to connect harvest to home while supporting grower livelihoods.

Ebbesen Woodworking operates from Warrenville, Illinois, as a one-person artisan workshop specializing in handcrafted outdoor bars and custom workbenches. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or founder’s name, but presents itself as a dedicated solo craftsmanship operation built around direct client communication and on-site installation.

The shop produces a curated line of backyard bars — including models such as The Main Spot, The Eyre Square, The Dartford, The Spanish Arch, The Sidekick, The Forest Hill, and The Storehouse — alongside three standard workbench sizes (8×2, 8×3, 8×4 feet) offered in fixed or mobile configurations. All pieces are fabricated in-house using pressure-treated lumber and weather-ready finishes, with a process that moves from design consultation through fabrication, delivery, and final setup. The workshop also accepts custom dimensions and accessory planning for both product lines.

The customer base consists of residential homeowners seeking permanent outdoor entertaining structures or durable shop furniture. Projects referenced in the company’s gallery include corner-friendly bars, grill-integrated layouts, dart-wing additions, and combined bar-storage footprints, as well as custom workbenches with pegboard, outlets, and varied depths. The service area covers the Warrenville region, with the company coordinating installation directly.

Ebbesen Woodworking emphasizes a single-craftsman model as its differentiator: every project is handled from first sketch to final install by the same builder, ensuring consistent fitment and direct communication. The company positions its straightforward quoting, builder-guided finish selection, and focus on real-world outdoor durability as the reasons clients choose its builds over mass-produced alternatives.

about:
Edge and End operates from Providence, Rhode Island, where it was founded in 2008 by Aaron Guttin. Guttin, a lifelong woodworker who built his first toolbox at age eight, brought nearly two decades of teaching experience and a professional background spanning general contracting, luthiery, shipwright work, cabinet making, and furniture design to the venture. The company began with a mission to blend craftsmanship with community impact.

The shop produces custom woodwork for residential and commercial clients, building every piece by hand to the customer’s specifications. Materials are locally sourced hardwoods, frequently repurposed, finished with natural, food-safe coatings. The operation emphasizes sustainable sourcing and handcrafted precision, though facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not publicly disclosed.

Clients include homeowners, businesses, and nonprofit organizations. Edge and End’s pilot partner, The Groden Network, is Rhode Island’s provider for individuals with autism and developmental disabilities; the company also works with The Met School to introduce students to trade careers. Each project is fabricated in collaboration with adults with disabilities and students, integrating workforce development into the production process.

Guttin frames the business as a vehicle for creating opportunity and connection. The company states that its distinguishing feature is the integration of vulnerable community members into the making of each piece, providing trade skills, meaningful employment, and supportive pathways—turning custom furniture into a mechanism for social impact.

about:
Eel River Brewing Company is based in Fortuna, California, in the heart of Humboldt County. The brewery's organic journey began in 1998 when a customer's request for a 'naked beer' free of harmful ingredients led to the creation of its first 100% organic ale, Amber Ale. By 1999, Eel River had become the first fully certified organic brewery in the United States, establishing itself as a pioneer in organic craft brewing.

The company produces a rotating lineup of organic ales, including India Pale Ale, California Blonde, Amber Ale, and Pilsner-style ale, along with hard seltzers. In addition to brewing, Eel River operates a pub and restaurant on-site, serving food such as smoked tri-tip, burgers, and wings, and sells branded apparel through its online shop. Its beers are distributed to retail stores across the region.

Eel River serves craft beer consumers through its taproom and retail distribution, as well as restaurant patrons seeking a dog-friendly patio and live music. The brewery's products are available in stores throughout Northern California, and its pub attracts both locals and visitors camping in the Humboldt area.

The brewery emphasizes its certified organic status, sustainable and eco-friendly practices, and a commitment to using pure ingredients without artificial additives. It positions itself as independent and locally sourced, brewing without compromise on flavor or environmental responsibility.

old_description: Independently owned global supplier, specializing in the design, development, and manufacture of thermoplastic and thermoset compounds.
about:
Electric Cable Compounds Inc (ECC) was established in 1988 in Naugatuck, Connecticut, as a privately owned and operated company. The business began as an independent global supplier focused on the design, development, and manufacture of thermoplastic and thermoset compounds for wire and cable applications.

ECC operates a non‑carbon‑black compounding facility that specializes in elastomeric, high‑performance rubber (EPR), polyolefin, and other specialty polymer‑based compounds and masterbatches. Its capabilities include custom compounding, toll mixing, formulation design, and the production of customized masterbatches with additives such as flame retardants, antioxidants, UV stabilizers, anti‑static agents, slip agents, and process aids. The site houses automated proprietary production lines with state‑of‑the‑art process control, as well as pilot‑scale equipment — Banbury mixers, twin‑screw extruders, a pilot wire line, and pilot compounding lines — supported by an on‑site laboratory staffed by chemists and technicians who conduct analytical testing (FTIR, DSC, TGA, rheology, LOI, flammability, thermal aging, moisture content, chemical compatibility, tensile/elongation/modulus, melt flow index, specific gravity, hardness) and extrusion trials.

The company’s primary market is wire and cable insulation and jacket materials, serving domestic and international customers. It also notes expansion into new markets beyond its core wire‑and‑cable focus.

ECC emphasizes its commitment to exceptional product quality, continuous improvement, and technical expertise, which it says yields compounds with a unique combination of flexibility, electrical performance, aging stability, and processability. Every box of material undergoes comprehensive testing prior to shipment to ensure consistency and reduce customer scrap.

name: Electrical Contractors Hawaii, Inc.
about:
Electrical Contractors Hawaii, Inc. (ECH) was founded in 1998 on the island of Oahu, with its headquarters in Kapolei, Hawaii. The company began as a high‑voltage electrical contractor focused on federal military projects, installing substations, communications, CATV, and overhead and underground distribution systems. It is a service‑disabled veteran‑owned small business (SDVOSB).

ECH provides full‑service electrical construction, installation, and maintenance for military, government, industrial, commercial, and residential projects. Its services cover electrical substations, switchgear, communications infrastructure, fiber optics, CATV, high‑voltage and medium‑voltage work, underground and overhead distribution, runway and highway lighting, building and historical renovations, pump stations, sewer lift stations, fitness centers, and office buildings. The firm also offers electrical design consulting, value engineering, and 24‑hour emergency service. ECH employs 50–100 electricians, linemen, groundmen, and support staff, and holds C‑10, C‑62, and C‑63 licenses in Hawaii plus a General Building and C‑13 electrical license in California and Arizona.

The company’s primary customers are U.S. military branches — Army, Navy, Air Force — and federal and state government agencies. Notable projects include electrical work at Pearl Harbor, Kaneohe Marine Corps Base, Camp Pendleton, Twenty‑Nine Palms, Hanscom AFB in Massachusetts, the Kahuku Wind Farm, Onizuka Village, Capehart/Earhart Military Housing, Ford Island, and the Red Hill Mauka project. ECH also serves commercial and industrial clients such as pump stations, sewer lift stations, airport hangars, and office buildings.

ECH emphasizes a zero‑accident safety culture, earning the Associated Builders and Contractors Platinum Safety Award eight of nine years from 2003 to 2011 and multiple Excellence in Construction Grand Awards for work on military installations. The firm highlights attention to detail, dedication to quality, and an experienced supervisory workforce as key differentiators.

about:
Electrical Power Products, operating as EP², was founded in the fall of 1988 in Des Moines, Iowa. Terry Nelson envisioned a better way to manufacture high-quality relay and control panels, and was joined by Tom David and Randy Dochterman within months. The three founders started in a 1,200-square-foot leased space with a commitment to quality that remains the company's highest priority.

Today EP² operates from a 310,000-square-foot facility with over 500 employees. The company produces complete power management systems for commercial and utility markets, including control enclosures, protective relay panels, and control systems for power generation, transmission, and distribution. Its capabilities span metal fabrication, powder coating, component mounting, wiring, and final testing, all governed by a five-point inspection process. The company reports serving 1,041 customers in the power industry.

EP² serves the commercial and utility power sectors, renewable energy facilities such as wind, solar, and geothermal installations, and the growing data center market. Its integrated modular control systems are delivered as "drop-in-place" units ready for immediate operation. The firm's engineering staff includes IEEE members, project managers, and estimating and procurement specialists.

The company differentiates itself through a quality management system that inspects products at five stages — after metal fabrication, powder coating, component mounting, wiring, and before shipment. Long-term employee retention, with many staff members staying 30-plus years, is cited as a reflection of workplace culture. An overhead crane enables weather-controlled handling of large enclosures, and the company emphasizes modernizing the nation's power grid and supporting reliable data center power.

name: Enable Injections, Inc.
old_description: Founded in 2010, Enable Injections is a healthcare innovation company committed to improving the patient treatment experience through the development and manufacturing of enFuse.
about:
Enable Injections, Inc. was founded in 2010 by medical device entrepreneur Mike Hooven in Cincinnati, Ohio. Hooven, who previously founded AtriCure and Enable Medical, established the company to develop a wearable drug delivery platform that could administer large volumes of medication subcutaneously. The privately held company has since raised more than $300 million in capital funding to advance its technology.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures the enFuse® system, a purely mechanical, hands-free wearable injector that delivers pharmaceutical and biologic therapeutics subcutaneously. The platform accommodates drug product viscosities ranging from 1 to 100 centipoise and eliminates the need for intravenous infusion, allowing patients to receive treatment through a simple injection under the skin. All design, development, and manufacturing operations are based at the company's Cincinnati headquarters.

Enable Injections serves the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, partnering with companies such as Sanofi, Sobi, and Aptar Digital Health to integrate enFuse with specific therapies. Sanofi’s subcutaneous Sarclisa (iscatuximab) has received regulatory approval in the U.S. and EU for administration via enFuse, while Sobi’s Aspaveli (pegcetacoplan) has obtained CE certification for use with the platform. The company also supports clinical trials and commercial launch planning for partnered combination products.

The company states its technology was driven by patient insights to improve the treatment experience, increase safety, and reduce the time, cost, and burden of chronic disease management. By removing needle-stick hazards and manual mixing steps, enFuse aims to enable patients to perform light to moderate activities during administration. The platform has been recognized by industry publications including Fierce Pharma and PM360 for its novel approach to large-volume subcutaneous delivery.

name: Erdman Auto Parts
old_description: Maryland Junkyards – Parts, Salvage, Towing, Repair, Recycling
about:
Based in Baltimore, Maryland, Maryland Junkyards has operated for more than three decades as a network of five salvage yards across the state. The company's locations include Erdman Auto Parts on Erdman Avenue in Baltimore, Redmonds Auto Parts in Pasadena, Marty's Auto Parts on Hollins Ferry Road, A-1 Auto Sales in Havre de Grace, and Stokes Auto Parts in Jefferson.

The business centers on used auto parts, automotive repair, towing, and vehicle recycling. Across its five facilities, the company stocks millions of parts covering most makes and models of cars and trucks, and offers installation services. Each year it recycles approximately 75,000 gallons of gasoline recovered from salvaged vehicles, using the filtered fuel in its own fleet and converting engine oils, transmission fluids, and gear lubricants to heat its warehouses; the remaining hulks are shredded for steel.

Customers range from individual vehicle owners seeking affordable replacement parts to repair shops needing specific components. The company buys junk vehicles directly from the public, providing free towing and cash on the spot, and also sells parts nationally through its eBay storefront. Its repair bays handle general automotive service for walk-in clients.

Maryland Junkyards emphasizes a one-stop-shop model: parts come with a limited replacement warranty, including lifetime coverage on alternators, starters, wiper motors, and heater blower motors, while engines and transmissions carry a minimum 30-day guarantee. The operation's recycling loop — reusing fluids and fuel on-site — is presented as both a cost saving and an environmental commitment.

about:
F&H Food Equipment Co. began in 1959 in St. Joseph, Missouri, when Wilbur Feagan and Paul Higley pooled their resources to hand-deliver dairy parts and supplies to local cheese plants and dairies. The company transitioned to employee ownership in 1995 when Feagan transferred the business to his workforce, and today it operates as a 100% employee-owned enterprise headquartered in Springfield, Missouri.

The company distributes sanitary processing equipment from brands such as SPX Flow, Rubber Fab, and Haynes Lubricants, while also providing in-house services including pump and valve repair, engineering and fabrication, CNC machining, custom stainless steel fabrication through its MecTec division, installation, and on-site training. F&H maintains 13 locations across the United States, with its Springfield headquarters housing warehouse, repair, fabrication, and machining operations, and serves customers internationally.

F&H serves processing facilities in food and beverage, dairy, beer/wine/spirits, pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical, personal care, pet food, and other hygienic and industrial applications. Its customer base ranges from small dairies to large-scale processors across the U.S. and abroad.

The company emphasizes that employee ownership aligns incentives toward collaborative problem-solving rather than individual commissions, and that long employee tenure preserves technical knowledge. F&H positions itself as a single source for equipment, parts, repair, engineering, and fabrication when off-the-shelf solutions fall short.

FORMA Custom Furniture operates from Madison, Wisconsin, where founders Molly and Jim Papadopoulos established the company to create long-lasting objects that encourage a slower pace of daily life. Factor 55 is based in Boise, Idaho. The company began as an engineering design firm whose staff brought extensive experience from the aerospace, defense, and semiconductor sectors, applying that rigor to a shared passion for off-road vehicle recovery.

Products are developed in-house using 3D CAD and Cosmos finite-element analysis, then validated through destructive testing at an instrumented test facility. Components are precision CNC-machined from 6000- and 7000-series aluminum alloys and 6Al-4V titanium.

The gear serves recreational off-road drivers (Jeep, truck, SUV), powersports users (UTV, ATV), and military/industrial customers. Example product families include the UltraHook XTV for side-by-sides, the FlatLink MultiMount for winch mounting, and the HD Recovery Kit Teton for heavy-duty trucks.

The company differentiates itself through its Closed System Winching™ methodology, which replaces traditional hooks with closed-link hardware to eliminate latch failure.

Factory Connection is headquartered in Prattville, Alabama. The company was founded in 1976 in Guntersville, Alabama, by Terry Scott and Kenny Littleton as a single 1,000-square-foot store. It remains family-owned and is now led by President and CEO Steve Williams alongside a team of executive managers, merchandisers, buyers, and regional and store personnel.

The retailer operates more than 200 stores across 16 states, encompassing over one million square feet of retail space. A state-of-the-art distribution center at the Guntersville corporate headquarters supports the network, enabling frequent shipment of new merchandise — often from limited-quantity purchases. Factory Connection buys from fashion manufacturers to offer brand-name and specialty-store apparel for juniors, misses, plus, men’s, accessories, shoes, and home décor at prices 25% to 70% below regular retail.

about:
Fiesta Plastics Inc. opened in 1988 in Mesa, Arizona, when founder Jack Thompson traded the title of his truck for a small injection molding machine after three decades in the plastics industry. Within months the machine was paid off and three more followed, laying the groundwork for a company that has grown steadily for over 30 years.

Today the 20,000-square-foot facility houses 19 injection molding machines ranging from 25 to 650 tons with shot sizes up to 7.5 pounds. The shop processes a wide range of thermoplastics including ABS, acetal, acrylic, HIPS, nylon, polycarbonate, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyurethane, PVC, and TPU. In-house tooling capabilities center on two Fadal high-speed machining centers, supporting mold production from simple mud sets to Class A tools, along with mold maintenance and repair. Product and mold design are handled in SolidWorks 2024, accepting Part, STEP, IGES, and STL files, while rapid prototyping is available via 3D printing in both plastic and metal materials.

The company serves customers needing a complete finished product, from micro-molded components to large complex assemblies. Its blog notes core competencies in mold building, injection molding, assembly, and value-added operations across a variety of part sizes and complexities.

Fiesta Plastics emphasizes a “Never Give Up” motto built on quality at an economical price, continual innovation, customer satisfaction as the top priority, and integrity in every interaction. The firm positions itself as a full-service partner rather than a molding shop alone, handling design, manufacturing, and delivery under one roof.

about:
Fine Wood Works is a family-owned cabinet shop based in Piedmont, Missouri. Founded in 2006 by Lucas and Sara Edgy, the business traces its roots to Lucas’s college years when he built bookcases and small cabinets for friends. By 2003 he was working full-time as a cabinetmaker in Piedmont, and two years later the couple opened Fine Wood Works. In 2006 they purchased 30 acres with a barn, which they remodeled into the current woodworking facility.

The company designs, builds, and installs custom cabinetry, furniture, architectural millwork, and front entrance systems for residential and commercial projects. Operating from an 11,000-square-foot shop expanded over the years — including a dedicated spray finishing room, sanding area, and countertop fabrication space — the team uses KCD software to create 3D cabinet presentations, a practice Lucas adopted early in the region. All work is completed in-house from design through installation.

Fine Wood Works serves homeowners undertaking kitchen, bathroom, and living-room remodels, as well as builders on new-home and commercial projects. Client testimonials reference projects in Town & Country, Missouri, and highlight collaboration with Lucas on custom islands, laundry rooms, and dining tables.

The shop emphasizes its guarantee to stand by craftsmanship and protect its reputation, promising to go the extra mile if quality falls short. Lucas notes that the business relies on customer referrals, and many clients return for additional projects.

Fire Mountain Solar LLC is based in Mount Vernon, Washington, and has been operating since 2001. The company was founded by the Nelson family, with co-owner Alana Nelson playing a key role in establishing the Solar Installers of Washington and serving in leadership positions with the Washington Solar Energy Industries Association. The business began with the design of an off-grid power system for the founders’ remote property, giving the team hands-on experience that still informs its work today.

Fire Mountain Solar serves homeowners, businesses, and remote-property owners across Washington and beyond. Project examples include off-grid cabins in the San Juan Islands, residential installations on Camano Island, and DIY support for a customer in La Grange, Texas. The company works with both new construction and retrofit projects, and offers remote consulting for clients outside its local service area.

The company distinguishes itself through its deep involvement in shaping Washington’s solar industry standards, its breadth of experience across simple and highly customized systems, and its philosophy of educating customers before selling. As a family-oriented, locally rooted business, it emphasizes long-term relationships and transparent communication, positioning itself as a partner rather than a transactional contractor.

about:
Florida Torque Converter Corporation operates from Cape Coral, Florida, at 906 SE 9th Street. The company specializes in remanufacturing torque converters for automotive applications.

The company remanufactures torque converters using a process it calls blueprinting, where each component is inspected, machined, and balanced to exceed original specifications. Technicians keep original parts together throughout the process to maintain matched sets. The facility stocks thousands of converters for immediate shipment and offers custom stall-speed calibration for performance applications. Products cover OEM replacement, diesel performance, high-performance, and Jeep-specific units.

Customers include retail buyers purchasing online, wholesale distributors through a dedicated program, and enthusiasts seeking performance upgrades for diesel, high-performance, and Jeep vehicles. The company serves the automotive aftermarket across the United States.

Florida Torque Converter differentiates itself by its matched-part remanufacturing method, lifetime warranty on all units, and the ability to customize stall speeds to a vehicle's power curve. The blueprinting process aims to reduce vibration and extend component life beyond factory standards.

The company serves convenience stores, travel centers, grocery retailers, quick-service restaurants, hospitality venues, K‑12 schools, colleges and universities, healthcare facilities, military installations, stadiums, micromarkets, and tradeshow environments. FCI was started to solve everyday operational challenges in foodservice. about:
Organized in 1975, FEPSCO Inc. (Food Equip Parts & Service Co) was established in Honolulu, Hawaii, to address a gap in the local market for factory replacement parts and repair services for commercial foodservice equipment. The company has operated continuously under the FEPSCO name since its founding.

FEPSCO acts as an authorized parts distributor and service provider for a broad roster of U.S. foodservice equipment manufacturers, including Chicago Faucets, T&S Brass, Dormont, Edlund, and Wells. From its Honolulu facility, the company maintains a large inventory of parts and accessories — ranging from faucets and drain assemblies to gas connectors and can opener components — and provides both in-warranty and out-of-warranty repair services. It also supplies customers across the Pacific Rim, with most outbound shipments sent overnight to destinations such as Guam, the Marianas, American Samoa, and U.S. military installations in Okinawa, Japan, and Korea.

The company serves commercial kitchen operators of all types: restaurants, cafeterias, hospital foodservice departments, and military galleys and messes. Its customer base extends to institutional facilities and U.S. Army and Air Force bases throughout the Pacific. FEPSCO also offers technical assistance by phone, fax, or email, drawing on factory-printed and electronic documentation.

FEPSCO was created to fill a void in Hawaii's foodservice supply chain, and its differentiation lies in its manufacturer-authorized status, deep inventory, and ability to ship overnight across the Pacific. The firm emphasizes ready access to factory technical data and a willingness to source hard-to-find items on request.
